newsitem.title: USA: J.P. Morgan files shelf for $1 bln in debt.
newsitem.headline: J.P. Morgan files shelf for $1 bln in debt.

text.p: J.P. Morgan & Co Inc said Wednesday it filed a shelf registration with the Securities and Exchange Commission to sell up to $1 billion in debt securities.
In addition, four business trusts formed by the company may also offer from time to time an undetermined amount of preferred securities, the filing said.
The debt securities will include senior subordinated and junior subordinated debentures, the filing said.
Net proceeds will be used for general corporate purposes, including the investment in equity and debt securities and interest-bearing deposits of subsidiaries, the filing said.
The New York-based company is a holding company for subsidiaries engaged globally in providing a wide range of financial services.
